sentences.en: With midterm elections only weeks away, pressure is high.

sentences.en: Democrats could lose their majority in the House and at least a dozen states where the governor is currently a Democrat could go Republican.

sentences.en: Heading into the midterms, the Democrats knew they had an uphill battle.
sentences.zh: 在进入中期选举之际，民主党人深知他们面临一场硬仗。

sentences.en: Midterms are always tough for the party that's currently in the White House.

sentences.en: You know, the price of gas has skyrocketed seemingly overnight.

sentences.zh: 萨福克大学与《今日美国》的最新民调显示，拜登总统的支持率已跌至38%的新低。

sentences.en: Not only does the party in power usually lose, they're also facing down a flagging economy and an unpopular president.
sentences.zh: 执政党不仅通常会输掉选举，他们还面临着低迷的经济和一位不受欢迎的总统。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Lisa Lair on one place where this democratic hope could live or die.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事丽莎·莱尔将带我们去看看这种民主希望可能存续或破灭的地方。

sentences.en: Michigan.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州。

sentences.en: It's Friday, November 4th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月4日，星期五。

sentences.en: Lisa, you've been reporting on abortion and the politics around abortion for a long time.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，你长期以来一直在报道堕胎问题以及围绕堕胎的政治。

sentences.en: And it's been a big issue in these midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 这已成为此次中期选举的一个重大议题。

sentences.en: You've told us that Michigan is really the place where we should look to understand how abortion will play in the midterMs.
sentences.zh: 你告诉我们，密歇根州确实是我们应该关注的地方，以了解堕胎问题将如何影响中期选举。

sentences.en: So, why Michigan?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么是密歇根州？

sentences.en: Well, so right now you have this patchwork of abortion laws across the country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，目前全国各地的堕胎法律参差不齐。

sentences.en: And you have 13 red states where abortion is mostly, if not completely, banned.
sentences.zh: 有13个红州，堕胎在很大程度上，甚至完全被禁止。

sentences.en: You have a whole bunch of blue states where the governors have taken steps to expand abortion access and make it easier for people to come from out of state into those places and get abortions.
sentences.zh: 还有一大批蓝州，州长们已采取措施扩大堕胎渠道，并为外州人士前往这些地方进行堕胎提供了便利。

sentences.en: And then you have this whole group of states in the middle that are politically perhaps a little more swingy where abortion rights really hang in the balance.
sentences.zh: 然后还有中间的一大群州，它们在政治上可能稍微摇摆不定，堕胎权在这些地方确实悬而未决。

sentences.en: And chief among them is Michigan.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的就是密歇根州。

sentences.en: In states like Michigan, Democratic governors have blocked anti-abortion legislation proposed by Republican legislatures.
sentences.zh: 在像密歇根州这样的地方，民主党州长阻止了共和党立法机构提出的反堕胎法案。

sentences.en: It has a Republican legislature and it currently has a Democratic governor.
sentences.zh: 它有一个共和党控制的立法机构，目前有一位民主党州长。

sentences.en: And that Democratic governor is up for re-election, Gretchen Whitmer.
sentences.zh: 而那位民主党州长格雷琴·惠特默正在竞选连任。

sentences.en: This Supreme Court ruling has said every state's going to have different rights for women in their state borders.
sentences.zh: 最高法院的这项裁决意味着每个州在其州界内将拥有不同的女性权利。

sentences.en: And it also has a trigger law, which is a 1931 law that would basically ban abortion in the state.
sentences.zh: 该州还有一项触发法，即1931年的一项法律，基本上会在该州禁止堕胎。

sentences.en: And in Michigan, we will go from being a pro-choice state to if this 1931 law goes into effect, we will have the most extreme law on the books in the country.
sentences.zh: 在密歇根州，如果这项1931年的法律生效，我们将从一个支持堕胎选择的州变成拥有全国最极端法律的州。

sentences.en: And so we are fighting like hell.
sentences.zh: 所以我们正在拼命抗争。

sentences.en: I have filed a lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 我已经提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: It hasn't been enacted.
sentences.zh: 它尚未实施。

sentences.en: It's been stayed by a lawsuit filed by Governor Whitmer.
sentences.zh: 它已被惠特默州长提起的诉讼所暂缓。

sentences.en: But it's on the books.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然在法律条文中。

sentences.en: So at this point, Michigan women still have access to abortion care.
sentences.zh: 所以目前，密歇根州的女性仍然可以获得堕胎护理。

sentences.en: But this injunction is in the process of being appealed.
sentences.zh: 但这项禁令正在上诉过程中。

sentences.en: So it's a precarious moment.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个岌岌可危的时刻。

sentences.en: And that's why we've got to continue this fight.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们必须继续这场斗争。

sentences.en: So the first way abortion is on the ballot is with this gubernatorial election.
sentences.zh: 所以堕胎问题出现在选票上的第一个方式就是这次州长选举。

sentences.en: If a Democrat wins that race, Gretchen Whitmer, she continues to fight against that law.
sentences.zh: 如果民主党人格雷琴·惠特默赢得竞选，她将继续对抗那项法律。

sentences.en: If the Republican, Tudor Dixon, wins the race, it's far more likely that that law goes into effect.
sentences.zh: 如果共和党人图多尔·迪克森赢得竞选，那项法律生效的可能性要大得多。

sentences.en: My position on abortion is clear.
sentences.zh: 我在堕胎问题上的立场很明确。

sentences.en: I am pro-life with exceptions for life of the mother.
sentences.zh: 我支持生命权，但有例外情况，即母亲生命受到威胁时。

sentences.en: But I understand that this is going to be decided by the people of the state of Michigan or by a judge.
sentences.zh: 但我明白，这将由密歇根州的人民或法官来决定。

sentences.en: So that's the first way that abortion is effectively on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 所以这是堕胎问题实际上出现在选票上的第一种方式。

sentences.en: That's the first way.
sentences.zh: 这是第一种方式。

sentences.en: Then there's this other way.
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一种方式。

sentences.en: And this is what makes Michigan a bit more unique.
sentences.zh: 这就是让密歇根州显得有些独特的地方。

sentences.en: There's Proposal 3 or Prop 3.
sentences.zh: 有“第3号提案”或“Prop 3”。

sentences.en: And that is a ballot measure that would essentially establish a right to reproductive freedom is how they phrase it in the state's constitution.
sentences.zh: 这是一项投票提案，本质上会在州宪法中确立所谓的生殖自由权。

sentences.en: So it would put the Roe standard back in place in Michigan and go a little further.
sentences.zh: 它将使“罗诉韦德案”的标准在密歇根州恢复，并更进一步。

sentences.en: It would enshrine a right to make and carry all decisions about things like pregnancy and contraception and infertility and sterilization, miscarriage management,
sentences.zh: 它将把关于怀孕、避孕、不孕不育、绝育、流产管理等事项做出和执行所有决定的权利写入宪法，

sentences.en: all the things that Democrats and liberals and people who support abortion rights are worried about in this post-Roe environment.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是民主党人、自由派以及支持堕胎权的人们在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后的环境中担心的事项。

sentences.en: Now, it's not the only state with this kind of initiative.
sentences.zh: 现在，它并不是唯一一个有此类倡议的州。

sentences.en: California has one on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州选票上也有一个。

sentences.en: Vermont has one on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 佛蒙特州选票上也有一个。

sentences.en: But it is the only swing state with this kind of initiative.
sentences.zh: 但它是唯一一个有此类倡议的摇摆州。

sentences.en: So it really is a test of how voters in competitive areas feel in some ways about abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 所以这在某种程度上确实是对竞争地区选民如何看待堕胎权的一次考验。

sentences.en: So abortion is on the ballot in Michigan because if the Republican wins, they could very easily have an abortion ban come January, right?
sentences.zh: 所以堕胎问题在密歇根州的选票上，是因为如果共和党人获胜，他们很容易在明年一月就实施堕胎禁令，对吧？

sentences.en: And then abortion, of course, is also literally on the ballot in Prop 3.
sentences.zh: 当然，堕胎问题也确实直接出现在“第3号提案”的选票上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Democrats know there is this population of people in the state, largely Democrats, some independent voters as well, who support abortion rights.
sentences.zh: 所以民主党人知道州里有这样一群人，主要是民主党人，也有一些独立选民，他们支持堕胎权。

sentences.en: And they suspect that they will come out and vote in favor of Prop 3 in November.
sentences.zh: 他们推测这些人会在11月出来投票支持“第3号提案”。

sentences.en: And then Democrats hope that they will also vote Democratic down the rest of the ticket.
sentences.zh: 然后民主党人希望他们也会在其余的选票上投给民主党。

sentences.en: OK.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So in terms of the politics then, it sounds like that Democrats are thinking that, number one, abortion should be protected in the state constitution.
sentences.zh: 那么就政治而言，听起来民主党人认为，第一，堕胎权应该在州宪法中得到保护。

sentences.en: But number two, Democrats should be using abortion as a motivator in the midterms, which, of course, is what the Republicans have been doing for years, right?
sentences.zh: 但第二，民主党人应该利用堕胎问题作为中期选举的激励因素，这当然也是共和党人多年来一直在做的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 他看到了将福音派选民转化为共和党坚定票仓的潜力。

sentences.en: Can they employ the same playbook and use abortion and the popularity of abortion rights to their advantage?
sentences.zh: 他们能否沿用同样的策略，利用堕胎议题以及堕胎权的受欢迎程度来为自己争取优势？

sentences.en: Will this threat to abortion rights not only bring people out to vote to support abortion rights and bring back some kind of Roe-like standard in their state,
sentences.zh: 这种对堕胎权的威胁，不仅会促使人们投票支持堕胎权，并在各自州内恢复某种类似“罗诉韦德案”的标准，

sentences.zh: 它是否还会促使人们出来投票，支持所有民主党候选人，甚至让那些过去可能投给共和党的人转而支持民主党？

sentences.en: in the way that it really unified and brought out evangelicals for Republicans for so many decades?
sentences.zh: 就像几十年来它成功团结并动员福音派支持共和党那样？

sentences.en: So Jess and I wanted to see how people on the ground who are connecting the issue of abortion rights to Democratic candidates on the ticket, how they're doing.

sentences.zh: 谁想先来？

sentences.en: So we are just going around giving out some information about Props 1, 2, and 3 for November's election.

sentences.en: And the thing they lead with, which is really interesting, is the proposals, including Prop 3.
sentences.zh: 他们开场切入的话题非常有趣，就是这些提案，包括第3号提案。

sentences.en: Women's Reproductive Rights Proposal 3, very important one this year.
sentences.zh: “女性生殖权利第3号提案”，这是今年非常重要的一项。

sentences.en: Needs not explaining.
sentences.zh: 无需多言。

sentences.en: Women deserve to have the rights to determine what they do with their bodies when it comes to pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 女性理应有权决定自己在怀孕方面的身体自主权。

sentences.en: Miscarriage management and infertility, sterilization, you name it.
sentences.zh: 无论是流产护理、不孕不育、绝育手术，等等。

sentences.en: And this is really the pitch they're making to voters, that if you support Prop 3, you should support these Democratic candidates, too.
sentences.zh: 这确实是他们向选民推销的重点：如果你支持第3号提案，你也应该支持这些民主党候选人。

sentences.en: We also have some information here about the candidates that we are endorsing that feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我们这里还有一些关于我们支持的、持同样观点的候选人的信息。

sentences.en: Have you had a chance to take a look at any of these candidates?
sentences.zh: 你有机会看一看这些候选人吗？

sentences.zh: 角色扮演练习结束后，负责指挥这次外勤行动的凯西·科普问大家：

sentences.en: Can anyone explain to me why, again, we lead with the issues Dylan did, proposals 1, 2, and 3?
sentences.zh: 有人能再解释一下，为什么我们以迪伦刚才提到的议题——第1、2、3号提案——作为开场吗？

sentences.en: Why do we do that first?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们先做这个？

sentences.en: Can anyone explain to me?
sentences.zh: 有人能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Because they're not really partisan.
sentences.zh: 因为它们并不是真正的党派议题。

sentences.en: I mean, everyone needs explaining, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为每个人都需要解释。

sentences.en: Precisely.
sentences.zh: 说得对。

sentences.en: Now, remember, many folks that we're talking to do not understand or not necessarily know who all the candidates are from top down.
sentences.zh: 记住，我们交谈的许多人并不了解，或者不一定知道从上到下所有的候选人是谁。

sentences.en: Many people have heard of Whitmer.
sentences.zh: 很多人听说过惠特默。

sentences.en: Some people have heard of Benson.
sentences.zh: 有些人听说过本森。

sentences.en: Even fewer people have heard of the state legislative candidates.
sentences.zh: 听说过州立法机构候选人的人就更少了。

sentences.en: But in order to connect our issues to the candidates, we are getting people to say yes to supporting these super popular issues.
sentences.zh: 但为了将我们的议题与候选人联系起来，我们让人们先对这些极受欢迎的议题说“是”。

sentences.en: Proposal 3, women's rights.
sentences.zh: 第3号提案，女性权利。

sentences.en: Proposal 2, voting rights.
sentences.zh: 第2号提案，投票权。

sentences.en: These are the issues that we connect then to the candidates.
sentences.zh: 这些就是我们随后与候选人挂钩的议题。

sentences.en: It's because the candidates that we support support those issues and those ballot proposals will not get instituted without their allies in office.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们支持的候选人也支持这些议题，而如果没有他们在任，这些投票提案就无法落实。

sentences.en: So that's why we do that, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我们这样做的原因，对吧？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they're finding that this is kind of working for them.
sentences.zh: 他们发现这种方法对他们来说挺管用的。

sentences.en: Have you guys had much luck with convincing people to vote Democrat using Prop 3?
sentences.zh: 你们在用第3号提案说服人们投票给民主党方面有很多收获吗？

sentences.en: Most definitely.
sentences.zh: 绝对有。

sentences.en: Most definitely, yes.
sentences.zh: 绝对有，是的。

sentences.en: People who would, when the first question we ask is, do you plan to vote in November?
sentences.zh: 当我们问的第一个问题是“你打算在11月投票吗？”时，有些人会回答没有。

sentences.en: And their answer is no.
sentences.zh: 他们的回答是“不”。

sentences.en: I'll ask why.
sentences.zh: 我会问为什么。

sentences.en: And they'll say it's just not what they care about right now.
sentences.zh: 他们会说那不是他们现在关心的事。

sentences.en: They've never really been interested in politics.
sentences.zh: 他们从来没对政治感兴趣过。

sentences.en: And I said, well, do you know about the proposals that are on the ballot?
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，你知道选票上有这些提案吗？

sentences.en: And I'll explain the proposals.
sentences.zh: 然后我会解释这些提案。

sentences.en: And their eyes get big.
sentences.zh: 他们的眼睛都亮了。

sentences.en: And they're going like, oh, okay, when is the election?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，好的，选举是什么时候？

sentences.en: And I'll highlight it on the information that we're giving to them.
sentences.zh: 我会把我们给他们的信息资料上的日期标出来。

sentences.en: And they're going to go, okay, I'm going to make sure that I get this done.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，好的，我一定会去投票。

sentences.en: And we get more people going, I didn't know it was that kind of thing, because they're looking at taking away more of our rights.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的人说，我不知道还有这种事，因为他们正盯着要剥夺我们更多的权利。

sentences.en: And we can't afford to let them do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不能让他们得逞。

sentences.en: So more people have told me, yes, I haven't voted in a while, but I'm definitely going to go out now.
sentences.zh: 所以更多人告诉我，是的，我有一阵子没投票了，但我现在一定会去投。

sentences.en: At the same time, because of the headwinds facing Democrats, Prop 3 has become sort of a lifeline for them.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，由于民主党面临的阻力，第3号提案已成为他们的救命稻草。

sentences.en: Without Prop 3 on the ballot, where do you think you would be at this point in the election?
sentences.zh: 如果没有第3号提案在选票上，你觉得你们现在会处于什么境地？

sentences.en: That is a great question, Jess.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，杰斯。

sentences.en: You know, because that would make our jobs so much harder, because then we would just have to focus on these issues that for 80% of the population, they don't know anything
sentences.zh: 因为那会让我们的工作难得多，因为那样我们就只能专注于那些80%的人口根本不了解的议题，

sentences.en: really about politicians beyond like the top of the ticket.
sentences.zh: 除了选票最顶端的候选人之外，他们对政客几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: So having to argue to someone, things that Gretchen Whitmer has accomplished in her four
sentences.zh: 所以要向别人论证格雷琴·惠特默在过去四年州长任期内取得的成就，

sentences.en: years as governor, are great preschool education, car insurance, things like that are awesome that she has accomplished.
sentences.zh: 比如优质的学前教育、汽车保险，这些成就都很棒。

sentences.en: But for most people that aren't focused on the politics of the state legislature, they're just like looking at the economy and are worried about their investments.
sentences.zh: 但对于大多数不关注州议会政治的人来说，他们只关注经济，担心自己的投资。

sentences.en: They're worried about housing, they're worried about groceries and gas.
sentences.zh: 他们担心住房，担心食品杂货和汽油价格。

sentences.en: And having to overcome those issues without the larger things at play, such as voting rights,
sentences.zh: 如果选票上没有投票权、女性权利、生殖自由这些更大的议题，

sentences.en: such as women's rights, reproductive freedom, those are the issues that we would really be struggling to convince people if we didn't have those on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 我们真的很难说服人们去投票。

sentences.en: He basically says that without Prop 3, Democrats would be in a much harder position in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 他基本上是说，如果没有第3号提案，民主党在密歇根州的处境会艰难得多。

sentences.en: Do you think like Democrats would be doing better nationally if there were more Prop 3s?

sentences.en: Oh, definitely.

sentences.en: You know, becoming the kind of political boon that it has been to Republicans all these decades.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这变成了几十年来共和党一直享有的那种政治红利。

sentences.en: But I guess the question to me is, how powerful a tool will it actually be?
sentences.zh: 但我认为对我来说的问题是，它到底会是一个多强大的工具？

sentences.zh: 它的影响有多深远？

sentences.zh: 她让我们在他们睡觉前去拜访，大家都知道那是去别人家最混乱的时候。

sentences.en: Hello!
sentences.zh: 你好！

sentences.en: Hi!
sentences.zh: 嗨！

sentences.en: What's your name?
sentences.zh: 你叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Colin.
sentences.zh: 科林。

sentences.en: Colin.
sentences.zh: 科林。

sentences.en: My name is Charlotte.
sentences.zh: 我叫夏洛特。

sentences.en: Charlotte!
sentences.zh: 夏洛特！

sentences.en: Nice to meet you guys.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你们。

sentences.en: What are you guys reading?
sentences.zh: 你们在读什么书？

sentences.en: I had a terrible...
sentences.zh: 我经历了一件可怕的……

sentences.en: This book is about Snuggle Bear.
sentences.zh: 这本书是关于拥抱熊的。

sentences.en: It's about...
sentences.zh: 它是关于……

sentences.en: It's about...
sentences.zh: 它是关于……

sentences.en: I look sad and then Snuggle Bear and give him nice big hugs.
sentences.zh: 我看起来很难过，然后拥抱熊给了我一个大大的拥抱。

sentences.en: Aw!
sentences.zh: 噢！

sentences.en: So the bear gives hugs.
sentences.zh: 所以这只熊会给人拥抱。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When I cry, I hug my mom.
sentences.zh: 当我哭的时候，我会抱我的妈妈。

sentences.en: And after a little while, her husband brought the kids up to bed.
sentences.zh: 过了一会儿，她丈夫带着孩子们上楼睡觉去了。

sentences.en: I'm going to leave you guys to it.
sentences.zh: 我就不打扰你们了。

sentences.en: It's nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴认识你们。

sentences.en: And then we were able to sit down with Amanda at her dining room table.
sentences.zh: 随后我们得以在阿曼达的餐桌旁坐下来交谈。

sentences.en: So are you...
sentences.zh: 那么你是……

sentences.en: Would you describe yourself as a Democrat, Republican, Independent?
sentences.zh: 你会如何形容自己？是民主党人、共和党人还是独立人士？

sentences.en: I think I would kind of label myself as an Independent.
sentences.zh: 我想我会把自己归类为独立人士。

sentences.en: I've voted Republican and Democrat in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 我过去既投过共和党，也投过民主党。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: My family is all very Republican.
sentences.zh: 我的家人全都是坚定的共和党人。

sentences.en: That's kind of where I'm from here in West Michigan is definitely Republican leaning.
sentences.zh: 我来自密歇根州西部，这里的人确实倾向于共和党。

sentences.en: So that's kind of all I knew.
sentences.zh: 所以我所知道的也就这些了。

sentences.en: And her story starts pretty close to where she lives now.
sentences.zh: 她的故事开始于离她现在住处不远的地方。

sentences.en: She grew up about 30 minutes away in Ionia County.
sentences.zh: 她在约30分钟路程外的爱奥尼亚县长大。

sentences.en: I'm from kind of a small farming community.
sentences.zh: 我来自一个小小的农业社区。

sentences.en: It's a very conservative area.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常保守的地区。

sentences.en: We grew up kind of going to church.
sentences.zh: 我们从小就是去教堂长大的。

sentences.en: My mom, you know, would bring us along and everything.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈，你知道，会带着我们去参加各种活动。

sentences.en: And her family is just kind of standard Republican.
sentences.zh: 她的家庭属于那种标准的共和党家庭。

sentences.en: They vote for Republicans, but they're not super political.
sentences.zh: 他们投票给共和党，但并不是特别热衷于政治。

sentences.en: She said in her family they never really talked about politics at all.
sentences.zh: 她说在家里他们几乎从不谈论政治。

sentences.en: But conservative values were kind of just in the air.
sentences.zh: 但保守的价值观在那种环境下是潜移默化的。

sentences.en: Growing up, I definitely would probably say I was pro-life.
sentences.zh: 在成长过程中，我肯定会说我是反堕胎的。

sentences.en: What did you think an abortion was growing up?
sentences.zh: 你小时候认为堕胎是什么？

sentences.en: I mostly thought it was, you know, people that just didn't want to have a baby.
sentences.zh: 我大多认为那只是，你知道，人们单纯不想生孩子而已。

sentences.en: I'm a firstborn, so I felt like I had to kind of be the good girl, the good example for my siblings.
sentences.zh: 我是长女，所以我感觉自己必须做一个好女孩，为弟妹们树立好榜样。

sentences.en: I guess I personally thought that, like, I would never have an abortion.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时个人认为，我是绝对不会去堕胎的。

sentences.en: So that's how she grew up, and that's how she was for many, many years, until a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 这就是她的成长经历，也是她多年来的想法，直到几年前。

sentences.en: And something unexpected started happening.
sentences.zh: 然后，意想不到的事情开始发生了。

sentences.en: When my husband and I, we had our first son, and when we were starting to try for our second child.
sentences.zh: 我和丈夫有了第一个儿子，之后我们开始尝试要第二个孩子。

sentences.en: She has her son in 2015.
sentences.zh: 她在2015年生下了儿子。

sentences.en: She gets pregnant pretty easily.
sentences.zh: 她怀孕的过程相当顺利。

sentences.en: And then two years later, in 2017, she starts trying for a second kid.
sentences.zh: 两年后的2017年，她开始尝试怀第二个孩子。

sentences.en: Everything was seeming to be on track and go well.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都在按计划进行，进展顺利。

sentences.en: And then we went to our 12-week appointment where we were excited to hear the heartbeat, and there was no heartbeat.
sentences.zh: 然后我们去做了12周的产检，本以为能听到心跳，结果却没有心跳。

sentences.en: So they did an ultrasound and discovered that there was no baby actually growing in the sack.
sentences.zh: 医生做了超声波检查，发现孕囊里并没有胎儿在发育。

sentences.en: So I took the pill.
sentences.zh: 所以我吃了药。

sentences.en: My body wasn't starting to miscarry on its own, so I took the medicine that they give you if you were to go have an abortion, just to expel everything from my body.
sentences.zh: 我的身体没有自行流产，所以我服用了医生给的药——也就是堕胎药，只是为了把体内的组织排出来。

sentences.en: And so she's having a miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 于是她经历了流产。

sentences.en: The doctor gives her an abortion pill to help expel the fetal tissue, but she starts bleeding a lot.
sentences.zh: 医生给她开了堕胎药来帮助排出胎儿组织，但她开始大量出血。

sentences.en: I actually passed so much blood that I passed out, and my husband had to call 911 and was taken to the hospital.
sentences.zh: 我当时失血过多以至于昏倒了，我丈夫不得不拨打911，我被送进了医院。

sentences.en: When I was at the hospital, they did an emergency DNC because not everything was passing like it should be.
sentences.zh: 在医院里，他们为我做了紧急刮宫手术，因为有些组织没有像预期的那样排出来。

sentences.en: So that was extremely traumatic.
sentences.zh: 那段经历极其痛苦。

sentences.en: And she's rushed to the hospital where they do an emergency DNC.
sentences.zh: 她被紧急送往医院接受了刮宫手术。

sentences.en: And this is the procedure.
sentences.zh: 这就是那个手术。

sentences.en: It's a surgical procedure where the doctors extract the fetal tissue that hasn't been expelled by your body.
sentences.zh: 这是一种外科手术，医生会取出身体没有自行排出的胎儿组织。

sentences.en: It's also the procedure that's used in abortions.
sentences.zh: 这也是堕胎所使用的手术。

sentences.en: But this is a miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 但这是流产。

sentences.en: There's no heartbeat detectable or no fetal activity.
sentences.zh: 没有检测到心跳，也没有胎儿活动。

sentences.en: But fundamentally, it's the same procedure.
sentences.zh: 但从根本上说，手术过程是一样的。

sentences.en: I was going for the beta blood work, and...
sentences.zh: 我当时去做了β-HCG血液检查，然后……

sentences.en: About six months later, she gets pregnant again.
sentences.zh: 大约六个月后，她又怀孕了。

sentences.en: And went, I think, two or three times, and then my numbers started to drop.
sentences.zh: 我想我去了两三次，然后我的数值开始下降。

sentences.en: So I knew it was happening again.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道同样的事情又发生了。

sentences.en: And she has another miscarriage.
sentences.zh: 她又流产了。

sentences.en: And as she's recounting her third miscarriage...
sentences.zh: 当她讲述第三次流产时……

sentences.en: I'm trying to think here.
sentences.zh: 我在努力回想。

sentences.en: I'm trying to think, like, when, like, month-wise this was.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这大概是在哪个月份发生的。

sentences.en: It becomes clear she couldn't remember the date.
sentences.zh: 很明显她记不清日期了。

sentences.en: Let me check my notes on this, because I do have...
sentences.zh: 让我查查我的笔记，因为我确实有……

sentences.en: This is how I, like...
sentences.zh: 这就是我，像……

sentences.en: Oh, it's a calendar.
sentences.zh: 噢，这是个日历。

sentences.en: ...kept track of everything, so...
sentences.zh: ……记录下了一切，所以……

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: This calendar basically represents our two and a half years of infertility.
sentences.zh: 这个日历基本上记录了我们两年半的不孕经历。

sentences.en: And just kind of helps me remember those pregnancies that we had.
sentences.zh: 它能帮我记住我们经历过的那些怀孕过程。

sentences.en: Amanda ended up having five miscarriages, back-to-back, between 2017 and 2019.
sentences.zh: 阿曼达在2017年到2019年间连续经历了五次流产。

sentences.en: Wow, five miscarriages.
sentences.zh: 哇，五次流产。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a lot.
sentences.zh: 是的，这确实很多。

sentences.en: And then in 2019, we got pregnant, my seventh pregnancy, and that resulted in my daughter.
sentences.zh: 然后在2019年，我们怀孕了，这是我的第七次怀孕，最终生下了我的女儿。

sentences.en: So...
sentences.zh: 所以……

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Did you keep this real-time, or...?
sentences.zh: 你是实时记录的吗，还是……？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And so this calendar, which is really an extraordinary log of this really difficult period of her life,
sentences.zh: 所以这个日历，实际上是一份关于她人生中这段极其艰难时期的非凡记录，

sentences.en: forms this picture of this transformation, where her views on abortion begin to change.
sentences.zh: 勾勒出了一场转变，她的堕胎观也随之开始改变。

sentences.en: And I point to the start of that calendar.
sentences.zh: 我指着日历的开头问她。

sentences.en: So here, in January 1, 2017, you're pro-life?
sentences.zh: 那么在这里，2017年1月1日，你是反堕胎的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then here...
sentences.zh: 然后在这里……

sentences.en: Well, here, it looks like September 14, 2019.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这里看起来是2019年9月14日。

sentences.en: Are you still pro-life at that point?
sentences.zh: 那时候你还是反堕胎的吗？

sentences.en: Are you...
sentences.zh: 你是……

sentences.en: Have your views started...
sentences.zh: 你的观点开始……

sentences.en: My views had started to change, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我的观点确实开始改变了。

sentences.en: I definitely am pro-choice right now.
sentences.zh: 我现在绝对是支持堕胎权的。

sentences.en: I guess I had never really, you know, in medical terms, a miscarriage is labeled as an abortion.
sentences.zh: 我想我以前从未真正意识到，在医学术语中，流产也被标记为堕胎。

sentences.en: I didn't know that before I went through, you know, what we went through.
sentences.zh: 在我经历这一切之前，我根本不知道这一点。

sentences.en: And around the time that she's going through this intensely difficult period of her life,
sentences.zh: 就在她经历人生中这段极其艰难的时期时，

sentences.en: Donald Trump is president, and she doesn't really like him.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普担任总统，而她并不怎么喜欢他。

sentences.en: Just how he treats people, for me, it's much more...
sentences.zh: 仅仅是他对待人的方式，对我来说，这更……

sentences.en: I'm seeing a lot of the extreme right wing.
sentences.zh: 我看到了很多极右翼的表现。

sentences.en: And so she starts to turn away from the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 于是她开始背离共和党。

sentences.en: And then in June, Roe falls.
sentences.zh: 然后在六月，《罗诉韦德案》被推翻了。

sentences.en: That was a huge changing point.
sentences.zh: 那是一个巨大的转折点。

sentences.en: I never...
sentences.zh: 我从没……

sentences.en: I never thought that we'd have to worry about this.
sentences.zh: 我从没想过我们还要担心这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, I juSt...
sentences.zh: 我是说，我只是……

sentences.en: I was in disbelief.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: Just knowing, like, if Roe would have been overturned a few years ago when we were going through all of this, and how my medical care would have changed.
sentences.zh: 只要想到，如果《罗诉韦德案》在几年前我们经历这一切时就被推翻了，我的医疗护理会变成什么样。

sentences.en: I just think it's insane that doctors are having to consult with lawyers before they can give this medical care that's needed right away.
sentences.zh: 我觉得医生在提供急需的医疗护理前必须先咨询律师，这简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Going through a miscarriage is so traumatic.
sentences.zh: 经历流产本身就已经非常痛苦了。

sentences.en: But when you would possibly have to prove that you're having a miscarriage and not having an abortion,
sentences.zh: 但如果你还要去证明你是在流产而不是在堕胎，

sentences.en: it just compounds the trauma.
sentences.zh: 这只会加剧这种创伤。

sentences.en: That moment when Roe fell, what was going through your mind as the thing that you didn't believe would happen, happened?
sentences.zh: 当《罗诉韦德案》被推翻的那一刻，当你认为不可能发生的事情真的发生了，你当时在想什么？

sentences.en: I started thinking about my daughter, and just I couldn't believe that this protection that her grandma had and I had was being taken away now.
sentences.zh: 我开始想到我的女儿，我简直无法相信她祖母和我曾经拥有的这种保护，现在竟然被剥夺了。

sentences.en: And it just scares me for what the future looks like for her and other young girls.
sentences.zh: 这让我对她和其他年轻女孩的未来感到恐惧。

sentences.en: I think it's like one in eight women are sexually assaulted in their life.
sentences.zh: 我想大约八分之一的女性一生中会遭受性侵犯。

sentences.en: In college, I was sexually assaulted.
sentences.zh: 我在大学时曾遭受过性侵犯。

sentences.en: And thankfully, it didn't result in a pregnancy.
sentences.zh: 谢天谢地，那次没有导致怀孕。

sentences.en: But, you know, if that were to happen to my daughter and she became pregnant, I would want her to have that option.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，如果这种事发生在我女儿身上，她因此怀孕了，我会希望她拥有选择权。

sentences.en: So this is Prop 3.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第3号提案。

sentences.en: We know how you're going to vote on that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道你会怎么投了。

sentences.en: What about the rest of the ticket?
sentences.zh: 那选票上的其他人选呢？

sentences.en: What are your plans?
sentences.zh: 你有什么打算？

sentences.en: I plan to vote straight Democrat down my ballot.
sentences.zh: 我打算在选票上全部投给民主党。

sentences.en: And so in this election, Amanda decided to vote Democratic.
sentences.zh: 于是，在这次选举中，阿曼达决定投票给民主党。

sentences.en: And she started talking to her family about politics and abortion, which is something that, as we said, she never really did before.
sentences.zh: 她开始和家人谈论政治和堕胎，正如我们所说，这是她以前从未做过的事。

sentences.en: My mom had posted something on her Facebook page kind of in support of Tudor Dixon, who is the Republican that's running for governor here in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈在她的Facebook页面上发了一些支持图德·狄克逊的内容，她是密歇根州共和党州长候选人。

sentences.en: And she has a very extreme pro-life stance on abortion.
sentences.zh: 她在堕胎问题上持非常极端的反堕胎立场。

sentences.en: She doesn't believe in abortion and rape or inceSt.
sentences.zh: 她甚至不赞成因强奸或乱伦而导致的堕胎。

sentences.en: I saw that on my mom's Facebook page.
sentences.zh: 我在我妈妈的Facebook页面上看到了这些。

sentences.en: And I called her up.
sentences.zh: 我给她打了电话。

sentences.en: And I was like, do you understand who Tudor Dixon is and what she stands for?
sentences.zh: 我说，你了解图德·狄克逊是谁以及她的立场吗？

sentences.en: And I just kind of went into, you know, do you understand that, like, on my medical record, it says that I've had five abortions?
sentences.zh: 我接着说，你知道吗，在我的医疗记录上，写着我做过五次“堕胎”吗？

sentences.en: If this would have happened a few years ago, like, I wouldn't have received the same care.
sentences.zh: 如果这种情况发生在几年前，我可能就无法得到同样的护理了。

sentences.en: And I think that really opened up her eyes to see that it could have affected me if it happened a few years ago.
sentences.zh: 我想这真的让她大开眼界，意识到如果这事发生在几年前，确实会影响到我。

sentences.en: And just knowing that she wants to make sure her granddaughters have that choice for themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且她也意识到，她想确保她的孙女们能拥有这种选择权。

sentences.en: When you told her that, like, how did she respond in that moment?
sentences.zh: 当你告诉她这些时，她当时是怎么回应的？

sentences.en: When you said these were on my record as abortions.
sentences.zh: 当你提到这些在我的病历上被标记为流产时。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I truly don't think that she knew that that's what miscarriages are often labeled on a medical record.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为她并不知道医疗记录中通常就是这样标注自然流产的。

sentences.en: So you managed to convince her to vote yes on Prop 3 to preserve and protect abortion rights in the state.
sentences.zh: 所以你成功说服了她投票支持第3号提案，以维护和保护该州的堕胎权。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So Amanda convinces her mom and several other family members, partially by talking about her own personal experience, she convinces them to vote yes on Prop 3.
sentences.zh: 阿曼达通过讲述自己的亲身经历，成功说服了她的母亲和其他几位家庭成员投票支持第3号提案。

sentences.en: And what about all these people you're talking to, the family, the friends, are they voting straight Democrat?
sentences.zh: 那么你交谈过的这些人，包括家人和朋友，他们会清一色地投票给民主党吗？

sentences.en: Probably most of them will vote Republican.
sentences.zh: 他们中的大多数人可能会投票给共和党。

sentences.en: But she fails to convince them to vote for Democrats down the ballot.
sentences.zh: 但她没能说服他们在选票上支持民主党候选人。

sentences.en: And this can show the limits of how the abortion issue could work for Democrats, that it might get people like Amanda to turn out and vote for them.
sentences.zh: 这显示了堕胎议题对民主党作用的局限性，它或许能让像阿曼达这样的人出来投票支持他们。

sentences.en: But for people like her mom, who's a Republican, it may not prompt them to overcome their partisan leanings and cross the aisle and vote for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但对于像她母亲这样身为共和党人的人来说，这可能不足以促使他们克服党派倾向，跨越党派界限去投票给民主党。

sentences.en: Amanda's mom didn't want to talk to us on tape.
sentences.zh: 阿曼达的母亲不想接受我们的录音采访。

sentences.en: But she explained over the phone that she's having a hard time bringing herself to vote for Democrats because she associates them with the defund the police movement.
sentences.zh: 但她在电话里解释说，她很难让自己投票给民主党，因为她将民主党与“削减警察经费”运动联系在一起。

sentences.en: And her son is a police officer.
sentences.zh: 而她的儿子是一名警察。

sentences.en: How do you react when you hear that people are going to be voting yes on Prop 3 and Republicans who could undo abortion protections?
sentences.zh: 当你听到人们投票支持第3号提案，却又投票给可能撤销堕胎保护的共和党人时，你有什么反应？

sentences.en: I personally don't understand how that goes together or makes sense.
sentences.zh: 我个人不明白这两者怎么能共存，或者说这怎么讲得通。

sentences.en: But I'm just hoping that Prop 3 will be strong enough to hold things together here in Michigan if it passes.
sentences.zh: 但我只是希望如果第3号提案通过，它能足够强大，在密歇根州维持住局面。

sentences.en: Are you trying to talk people into voting Democrat in addition to voting yes on Prop 3?
sentences.zh: 除了投票支持第3号提案外，你还在试图说服人们投票给民主党吗？

sentences.en: I feel like it's a very fine line.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这中间的界限非常微妙。

sentences.en: I feel like I've been having to be kind of careful and not push too hard.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我必须小心翼翼，不能逼得太紧。

sentences.en: I'm just worried about damaging relationships.
sentences.zh: 我只是担心会破坏人际关系。

sentences.en: The current political climate has been really hard for me, leaning Democratic when most of the people that are around me lean more Republican.
sentences.zh: 当前的政治气候让我感到非常艰难，因为我倾向于民主党，而我周围的大多数人都更倾向于共和党。

sentences.en: So yeah, it's been kind of—I kind of feel isolated and kind of alone.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这让我感到有点孤立，有点孤独。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: She's—my mom's been very, like, you're not going to change—you're not going to change my vote, you know.
sentences.zh: 她——我母亲一直很坚决，比如，你改变不了——你改变不了我的投票意向，你知道的。

sentences.en: I'm—I'm afraid if the Republicans get in control that they will do whatever they can to restrict abortion access to people in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 我——我很担心如果共和党人掌权，他们会竭尽所能限制密歇根州民众的堕胎途径。

sentences.en: The reality is that the politics around this, particularly this issue, abortion, which has been so controversial for so many decades, remain pretty fraught.
sentences.zh: 现实情况是，围绕这一议题，特别是堕胎这个几十年来一直极具争议的问题，其政治环境依然相当紧张。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: There's a limit to how much abortion is going to transform the electorate in these midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 堕胎议题在这些中期选举中能改变选民倾向的程度是有限的。

sentences.en: So for Amanda, that transformation is pretty complete.
sentences.zh: 所以对阿曼达来说，这种转变已经相当彻底了。

sentences.en: But for people in Amanda's family, they might be down for voting for abortion rights, but that doesn't mean they're suddenly voting for Democrats.
sentences.zh: 但对于阿曼达家里的其他人来说，他们可能愿意投票支持堕胎权，但这并不意味着他们会突然转而投票给民主党。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a limit to how far their views on abortion extend politically.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们的堕胎观点在政治上的延伸是有局限的。

sentences.en: So, Lisa, given that, I wonder if there's any chance that putting Prop 3 on the ballot could actually end up backfiring against Democrats.
sentences.zh: 那么，丽莎，鉴于此，我想知道将第3号提案列入选票是否反而可能对民主党产生反作用。

sentences.en: I mean, isn't it possible that, you know, number one, having Prop 3 on the ballot gives those Republican voters who support abortion rights a way to have it both ways,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，难道没有可能，第一，将第3号提案列入选票，让那些支持堕胎权的共和党选民可以两全其美吗？

sentences.en: voting for abortion but also voting for Republicans?
sentences.zh: 既投票支持堕胎，又投票给共和党？

sentences.en: And two, it could just as easily motivate that larger group of Republican voters, those who are against abortion, to go to the polls.
sentences.zh: 第二，这同样可能轻易地激励那一大群反对堕胎的共和党选民去投票。

sentences.en: And that, of course, would help Republicans.
sentences.zh: 而这当然会帮助共和党人。

sentences.en: So the split ticket thing, it's theoretically possible that it could have an impact.
sentences.zh: 所以这种“分裂投票”的情况，理论上确实可能产生影响。

sentences.en: And Amanda's family is doing that.
sentences.zh: 阿曼达的家人就在这样做。

sentences.en: And Jess and I heard of other people doing that, too.
sentences.zh: 杰斯和我听说其他人也在这样做。

sentences.en: It's probably not a huge group of people, given how polarized our political environment is.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我们政治环境的极化程度，这可能不是一个庞大的群体。

sentences.en: But we also know that Michigan is a really tight political state and that there is no way for Prop 3 to pass without picking up some measure of independent and moderate voters.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，密歇根州的政治形势非常胶着，如果不争取到一定比例的独立选民和温和派选民，第3号提案是不可能通过的。

sentences.en: There are just not enough diehard Democrats in Michigan to get it over the finish line.
sentences.zh: 密歇根州没有足够的铁杆民主党人来确保它顺利过关。

sentences.en: Now, whether those moderates and those independents then turn around and vote Republican, it's probably not a huge number of them.
sentences.zh: 至于这些温和派和独立选民随后是否会转而投票给共和党，人数可能不会太多。

sentences.en: But there may be some.
sentences.zh: 但可能确实会有一些。

sentences.en: We just don't know how many because we've never operated in this post-Roe environment and we don't know how the politics are going to play out.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不知道具体有多少，因为我们从未在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻后的环境下运作过，我们不知道政治局势会如何演变。

sentences.en: We do know, though, from decades of politics that being against abortion consistently turns out Republicans.
sentences.zh: 不过，从几十年的政治经验中我们确实知道，反对堕胎一贯能动员共和党选民投票。

sentences.en: So there is a chance that Prop 3 could boost turnout for Republicans or at least keep it at the level it's been for all those decades when it comes to abortion, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以第3号提案确实有可能提高共和党的投票率，或者至少在堕胎问题上保持几十年来一贯的水平，也就是，你知道的，

sentences.en: fairly high.
sentences.zh: 相当高。

sentences.en: So I think the dream here for Democrats is that the same thing happens on their side, that the number of Amandas, people who are politically activated by abortion,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为民主党人的梦想是，同样的事情在他们那边发生，即阿曼达这类人的数量——那些因堕胎议题而产生政治觉醒的人——

sentences.en: who will turn out for Democrats again and again because they feel so passionate about this issue, that that number grows.
sentences.zh: 因为对这个议题充满热情，而会一次又一次地出来投票支持民主党，这个群体的人数会不断增长。

sentences.en: And look, that just takes time.
sentences.zh: 看，这需要时间。

sentences.en: The Democrats have only just started to talk about this because there wasn't a need to talk about it before Roe fell.
sentences.zh: 民主党人只是刚刚开始谈论这个问题，因为在“罗诉韦德案”被推翻之前，没有必要谈论它。

sentences.en: And look, few people really believe that the country would ever lose a federal right to an abortion.
sentences.zh: 而且，很少有人真的相信这个国家会失去联邦层面的堕胎权。

sentences.en: So it was a really hard case for Democrats to make.
sentences.zh: 所以这对民主党人来说是一个非常难打的牌。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not like a switch is suddenly flipped and someone who's a Republican becomes a Democrat, right?
sentences.zh: 这不像是一个开关突然被拨动，共和党人就变成了民主党人，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, there are so many different aspects to people's political identity right now, and they're all kind of fused together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们现在的政治身份有很多不同的层面，它们都融合在一起了。

sentences.en: And, you know, for someone to leave the Republican Party and go to the Democratic Party, it's a little bit kind of like, I don't know, immigrating to another country.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，对于一个人来说，离开共和党加入民主党，有点像，我不知道，移民到另一个国家。

sentences.en: It's like you have to leave the whole rest of your life behind.
sentences.zh: 就像你必须把余下的整个人生都抛在身后一样。

sentences.en: And it's also something Republicans who support abortion rights haven't really had to contend with ever because there was always Roe, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是支持堕胎权的共和党人从未真正需要面对的问题，因为一直有“罗诉韦德案”，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, they could just support abortion and vote Republican and be very confident that abortion would be protected because it was the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们可以既支持堕胎又投票给共和党，并且非常确信堕胎会受到保护，因为那是国家法律。

sentences.en: And now that's gone.
sentences.zh: 而现在这一切都没有了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And Michigan is the first test of this strategy, which is can abortion referendums supercharge Democratic activism and, you know, as a result, turnout?
sentences.zh: 密歇根州是这一策略的第一次测试，即堕胎公投能否激发民主党的积极性，并因此提高投票率？

sentences.en: Basically create an army of Amandas who will now vote in every midterm after midterm.
sentences.zh: 基本上创造出一支“阿曼达大军”，从此在每一次中期选举中都出来投票。

sentences.en: And also, even beyond that, can it flip some crucial measure of Republicans, get them to vote Democratic too, really, in some smaller sense,
sentences.zh: 而且不仅如此，它能否翻转一定比例的关键共和党人，让他们也投票给民主党，在某种程度上，

sentences.en: do basically what Republicans did in the late 1970s with evangelicals?
sentences.zh: 基本上做到共和党人在20世纪70年代末对福音派所做的事情？

sentences.en: And, you know, Democrats are optimistic about how it's going to go for them in Michigan, certainly more optimistic than they are in a lot of other parts in the country.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，民主党人对他们在密歇根州的胜算持乐观态度，当然比他们在全国其他许多地方要乐观得多。

sentences.en: And if they're successful in Michigan, you can bet that we're going to see a whole lot of copycats all across America in two years.
sentences.zh: 如果他们在密歇根州取得成功，你可以肯定，两年后我们会在全美看到大量的效仿者。

sentences.en: Lisa, thank you.
sentences.zh: 丽莎，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 今天，我们收到了以色列公民巨大的信任投票。

sentences.en: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's former prime minister, is set to become its next one after his right-wing bloc, led by his Likud party,
sentences.zh: 以色列前总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡在以其利库德集团为首的右翼阵营，

sentences.en: was projected to win a clear parliamentary majority in Israel's general election.
sentences.zh: 预计在以色列大选中赢得明确的议会多数席位后，即将成为下一任总理。

sentences.en: It was Israel's fifth election in four years and will be the first government to have a cohesive majority in Israel's parliamentary system since 2019.
sentences.zh: 这是以色列四年来的第五次选举，也将是自2019年以来第一个在以色列议会制度中拥有稳固多数席位的政府。

sentences.en: It will be one of the most right-wing governments in Israeli history.
sentences.zh: 这将是以色列历史上最右翼的政府之一。

sentences.en: An alliance of two religious ultra-nationalist parties, Jewish power and religious Zionism, placing once-marginal,
sentences.zh: 两个宗教超民族主义政党——“犹太力量”党和“宗教犹太复国主义”党的联盟，将曾经处于边缘地位的、
